Under these conditions the test describes the subject's internal coherence but constrains nothing external. The 3-of-26 result occurs because 23 of the 26 mutations preserve the subject's self-consistency (they are behaviour-preserving relative to the guard's tautological predicate), while only 3 break the specific tautological relation that the guard encodes.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The guard's predicate is not tautological relative to the subject; it encodes an independent specification","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 3-of-26 result is a false negative caused by a defect in the mutation-testing harness, not by tautological capture","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A test constrains its subject only when it can distinguish correct from incorrect behaviour, and a tautological test constrains nothing","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'tautological capture': a guard whose predicate is logically entailed by the subject's own code cannot distinguish between a correct subject and an incorrect one; it can only detect internal inconsistency. Mutations that introduce behaviour inconsistent with the guard's tautological predicate are constrained, while mutations that introduce consistent-but-wrong behaviour are merely described. The 3-of-26 distribution is the ratio of inconsistency-introducing mutations to consistency-preserving mutations.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
